_comment: Performance budgets, in gzipped KB as GitHub Pages serves them.
`ceiling` fails the check — it is today's value plus a little headroom, so nothing regresses.
`target` is where docs/INVARIANTS.md says we are going; it is reported, not enforced.
When a phase lands and the real number drops below `target`, LOWER the ceiling to the new
value + headroom in the same commit. That is how the ratchet works — a budget that is never
tightened is a budget that is never met.

boot.why: Everything needed to paint the hero and the first 25 cards. INTENT-2 (speed is the product).

search.why: Everything that must land before a text query can be answered. The single biggest lever on felt speed — see PERF-UX-AUDIT-2026-09-14.md S1 and E1. Phase 5 (E1) landed the token-prefix inverted index (data/qindex.bin) and REMOVED data/qtext.json from this list — the index is what finds a match now, qtext.json only renders the snippet and arrives after results are already on screen (DECISION-7), so it no longer gates the answer. Measured 2058.5 KB (post-I1) -> 1132.0 KB (post-E1), -926.5 KB / -45%. This is short of the audit's original 751/800 KB projection because that estimate (and its own addendum's 327.7 KB qindex.bin re-measurement) covered canonical questions only; production's qindex.bin also indexes ~3.1k copies' variant wording (a copy whose phrasing the deduped question doesn't faithfully contain) for search parity with what the substring scan used to match against QVARLC — dropping that coverage would silently stop matching those copies until qtext.json loads, which tools/perf/search-parity.mjs is built to catch. Measured cost of that parity: qindex.bin is 475.2 KB gzip (629.9 KB raw: 14,779 tokens, 8,102 questions + 3,103 variants), not the 327.7 KB canonical-only figure — see docs/DECISIONS.md DECISION-12. Ceiling carries ~63 KB headroom for corpus growth; target is a stretch goal for a future pass at trimming the translation table or postings encoding further, not assumed reachable without one.

app_js.why: DECISION-2 (no framework, no bundler). Phase 5 (E1) added the qindex.bin binary reader, the token-prefix query engine (prefix expansion, AND intersection, exact-phrase verification, substring fallback) and BM25-lite ranking — real core search functionality, not a feature that belongs behind a lazy-loaded module the way pdf.js/Tesseract do (DECISION-3), since every visitor who searches needs it. Measured 26.8 KB (pre-E1) -> 31.3 KB gzip. Phase 6 added R1's keyed card reconciliation (getCard()/reconcileBrowseList(), replacing box.innerHTML=''-and-rebuild — every browse visitor's list renders through this, not lazy-loadable) and R3's URL sync (syncUrl()/applyUrlToState(), likewise core). Measured 31.3 -> 33.4 KB gzip; ceiling ratcheted 33 -> 34 KB with ~0.6 KB headroom rather than trimming the comments a future session needs to understand why (DECISION-9/DECISION-13). If this creeps much past ~34 KB gz, something new was added that probably belongs in a lazy-loaded module instead.
